work.problem: Make the playbook the single canonical home of the seven shared agent skills, which today exist as copies in a private repository and in account-level skill stores that have drifted from each other.

findings.reason: The skills do not alter the journal or its append-only enforcement.
No control-catch metric or attribution changes.
No Jira issue shape or parser contract changes; the skills name a generic work tracker.
No Builder or price-table contract changes.
CAPA field validation stays intact; no register or journal schema changes.
No vendor sync, contract pin, or workflow changes; the skills are documents only.
No change to sync PR generation or its source name.
No promoted autonomy or changes to the evidence requirements; the skills restate that agent claims are not evidence.
No change to the governance baseline or its controls.
The work is recorded under KAN-123 and does not claim a ticket or finding closed.

lessons: One canonical copy per skill: the skills move here, and consumers point to a pinned commit instead of keeping copies.
Drift Prevention stays single-sourced in 00_UniversalStandards/09_Reuse_and_DRY.md; the skill points to it rather than restating it.
Commit this record before the skill files, as a separate first commit.
uncertainty: This record sits beside .kappa/KAN-123.json instead of replacing it, so the earlier record is kept; that departs from the one-file-per-ticket naming.
Whether the skills preserve existing behavior is checked by the owner against an equivalence table in the consuming repository's PR, not by a test.
